lines.raw: She has **one NMC number** everywhere, but each place is a different business with its own **PAN**, address and bills.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: **In one sentence: individual providers belong to organizations, organizations belong to larger ones, and each can work from several places, so provider data is a hierarchy, not a flat list.**
lines.say: In one sentence: individual providers belong to organizations, organizations belong to larger ones, and each can work from several places, so provider data is a hierarchy, not a flat list.

lines.raw: How providers are connected.
lines.say: How providers are connected.

lines.raw: Most US doctors do not work or sign contracts alone.
lines.say: Most U S doctors do not work or sign contracts alone.

lines.raw: They belong to a **group**, and the group belongs to something bigger:
lines.say: They belong to a group, and the group belongs to something bigger:

lines.raw: Group practice.
lines.say: Group practice.

lines.raw: Several doctors who share a business, a **TIN** and usually an office.
lines.say: Several doctors who share a business, a T I N and usually an office.

lines.raw: **Lakeside Surgical Group** is Dr. Lee's group.
lines.say: Lakeside Surgical Group is Doctor Lee's group.

lines.raw: Health system.
lines.say: Health system.

lines.raw: A larger organization that owns hospitals, clinics and groups, often under many TINs.
lines.say: A larger organization that owns hospitals, clinics and groups, often under many T I N's.

lines.raw: Many US hospitals belong to one.
lines.say: Many U S hospitals belong to one.

lines.raw: Hospital affiliation (privileges).
lines.say: Hospital affiliation (privileges).

lines.raw: Permission for a doctor to treat patients inside a hospital.
lines.say: Permission for a doctor to treat patients inside a hospital.

lines.raw: Dr. Lee works for Lakeside Surgical Group but has **privileges** at Lakeside General Hospital, which is why he could operate on Emily there.
lines.say: Doctor Lee works for Lakeside Surgical Group but has privileges at Lakeside General Hospital, which is why he could operate on Emily there.

lines.raw: IPA (Independent Practice Association).
lines.say: I P A (Independent Practice Association).

lines.raw: Independent doctors who join together only to sign contracts with insurers, while keeping their own practices.
lines.say: Independent doctors who join together only to sign contracts with insurers, while keeping their own practices.

lines.raw: A provider hierarchy, from biggest to smallest.
lines.say: A provider hierarchy, from biggest to smallest.

lines.raw: **Health system**. Identified by: A system ID kept by the insurer (there is no national one). Example: Imagine a system that owns several clinics in Austin. Answers: How much do we spend with this whole system?
lines.say: Health system. Identified by: A system I D kept by the insurer (there is no national one). Example: Imagine a system that owns several clinics in Austin. Answers: How much do we spend with this whole system?

lines.raw: **Business (tax entity)**. Identified by: **TIN**. Example: 74-5550101: Sunrise Family Clinic. Answers: Who gets paid? Which contract applies?
lines.say: Business (tax entity). Identified by: T I N. Example: 74-5550101: Sunrise Family Clinic. Answers: Who gets paid? Which contract applies?

lines.raw: **Organization**. Identified by: **Type 2 NPI**. Example: Sunrise Family Clinic, 1245987601. Answers: Which facility or group billed?
lines.say: Organization. Identified by: Type 2 N P I. Example: Sunrise Family Clinic, 1245987601. Answers: Which facility or group billed?

lines.raw: **Individual**. Identified by: **Type 1 NPI**. Example: Dr. Patel, 1043827165. Answers: Who did the work?
lines.say: Individual. Identified by: Type 1 N P I. Example: Doctor Patel, 1043827165. Answers: Who did the work?

lines.raw: **Location**. Identified by: Address (service location). Example: 120 Oak St, Austin. Answers: Where was the care given?
lines.say: Location. Identified by: Address (service location). Example: 120 Oak St, Austin. Answers: Where was the care given?

lines.raw: Same name, different businesses.
lines.say: Same name, different businesses.

lines.raw: Lakeside **Surgical Group** and Lakeside **General Hospital** share a town name but are **separate businesses** with separate TINs, separate contracts and separate claims.
lines.say: Lakeside Surgical Group and Lakeside General Hospital share a town name but are separate businesses with separate T I N's, separate contracts and separate claims.

lines.raw: That is why Emily got one claim from each.
lines.say: That is why Emily got one claim from each.

lines.raw: Never assume two providers are related because their names look alike: check the TIN and the affiliation data.
lines.say: Never assume two providers are related because their names look alike: check the T I N and the affiliation data.

lines.raw: Locations and addresses.
lines.say: Locations and addresses.

lines.raw: A provider record can carry **several addresses**, and each answers a different question:
lines.say: A provider record can carry several addresses, and each answers a different question:

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Service (practice) location**. What it is: Where patients are seen. A group may have many. Use it for: Directories, travel distance, "where was care given?".
lines.say: Service (practice) location. What it is: Where patients are seen. A group may have many. Use it for: Directories, travel distance, "where was care given?".

lines.raw: **Billing address**. What it is: Where the business sends claims from and receives payments. Use it for: Payment and tax forms.
lines.say: Billing address. What it is: Where the business sends claims from and receives payments. Use it for: Payment and tax forms.

lines.raw: **Mailing address**. What it is: Where letters go; can be a head office or a PO box. Use it for: Correspondence only.
lines.say: Mailing address. What it is: Where letters go; can be a head office or a P O box. Use it for: Correspondence only.

lines.raw: One NPI, many locations.
lines.say: One N P I, many locations.

lines.raw: An NPI does **not** change when a doctor works at several sites.
lines.say: An N P I does not change when a doctor works at several sites.

lines.raw: Dr. Lee keeps one Type 1 NPI whether he is at the group's office or operating at Lakeside General.
lines.say: Doctor Lee keeps one Type 1 N P I whether he is at the group's office or operating at Lakeside General.

lines.raw: To know **where** care happened, use the service location on the claim or the provider's location records, not the NPI.
lines.say: To know where care happened, use the service location on the claim or the provider's location records, not the N P I.

lines.raw: Emily's providers as a hierarchy.
lines.say: Emily's providers as a hierarchy.

lines.raw: provider_affiliation (example data; all IDs made up).
lines.say: provider_affiliation (example data; all I D's made up).

lines.raw: Notice that Dr. Lee appears **twice**: once as a member of his group (which pays him) and once with privileges at the hospital (where he works).
lines.say: Notice that Doctor Lee appears twice: once as a member of his group (which pays him) and once with privileges at the hospital (where he works).

lines.raw: Both are true at the same time.
lines.say: Both are true at the same time.

lines.raw: Relationships also have **start and end dates**, because doctors change groups.
lines.say: Relationships also have start and end dates, because doctors change groups.

lines.raw: Why it matters for data.
lines.say: Why it matters for data.

lines.raw: The level you group by changes the answer.
lines.say: The level you group by changes the answer.

lines.raw: Group by **Type 1 NPI** to compare individual doctors, by **TIN** to see which business was paid and which contract applied, and by **system** to see the insurer's biggest partners.
lines.say: Group by Type 1 N P I to compare individual doctors, by T I N to see which business was paid and which contract applied, and by system to see the insurer's biggest partners.

lines.raw: Value-based contracts are often signed with a **TIN** or a **system**, so these roll-ups decide whose members and costs are whose (lesson 6).
lines.say: Value-based contracts are often signed with a T I N or a system, so these roll-ups decide whose members and costs are whose (lesson 6).

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Doctors usually belong to a **group** (one TIN); groups and hospitals may belong to a **health system**.
lines.say: Doctors usually belong to a group (one T I N); groups and hospitals may belong to a health system.

lines.raw: **Hospital privileges** let a doctor work inside a hospital without being its employee.
lines.say: Hospital privileges let a doctor work inside a hospital without being its employee.

lines.raw: One provider can have several addresses: service location, billing and mailing.
lines.say: One provider can have several addresses: service location, billing and mailing.

lines.raw: The NPI stays the same at every site.
lines.say: The N P I stays the same at every site.

lines.raw: Affiliations have start and end dates, and one doctor can have several at once.
lines.say: Affiliations have start and end dates, and one doctor can have several at once.
